spec:
https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/tree/master/XLS-0074d-account-permissions
https://github.com/XRPLF/XRPL-Standards/tree/master/XLS-0075d-permission-delegation

This amendment is called `PermissionDelegation`

1. `DelegateSet` transaction is added so that a delegating account can give permission to delegated account to send transaction on his behalf.
```
{
    TransactionType: "DelegateSet",
    Account: "rDelegating......",
    Authorize: "rDelegated......",
    Permissions: [{Permission: {PermissionValue: "Payment"}}],
}
```
2. Ledger object `Delegate` is created, its keylet is hashed from delegating and delegated account.

3. optional common field `Delegate` is added, to indic

reviewCommentsList.author: ximinez
reviewCommentsList.body: Suggestion: Return `tesSUCCESS` here and in all the overrides, and remove the check for the presence of the field in the caller. That makes the caller simpler, but also gives more flexibility and only requires changing in one place if this check needs to be expanded in the future. I can't imagine any scenarios at the moment, but that doesn't mean it won't happen.

reviewCommentsList.author: ximinez
reviewCommentsList.body:
I am not a fan of modifying the transaction type with a hard coded magic number.

What is the problem with '0'? I haven't seen anything yet that makes '0' special or illegal. If not, then just use the unmodified value.

If there is a problem with '0', then use a new (static) modifier function in `Permissions`. e.g. `TypeToPermission(TxType type)`. All it needs to do is add 1, but this has the advantage of making it clear what's going on and why.

reviewCommentsList.author: ximinez
ximinez
reviewCommentsList.body:
I predict this list is going to get overlooked / forgotten _a lot_. I suggest reorganizing this to remove `isProhibited` and handle the check in the `Transactors`. Calling such a function directly from `STParsedJSON` would break all kinds of levelization / dependency rules, so here's what I suggest:
1. In `STParsedJSON`, don't check `isProhibited` at all. Just parse to the (modified) `TxType`.
2. Rename `Transactor::checkPermission` to `Transactor::checkPermissionBase`.
3. *Do not define `Transactor::checkPermission`.*
4. Now any `Transactor`-derived class that does not define `checkPermission` will fail to compile, including new ones added in the future.

For supported transaction types, de

reviewCommentsList.author: ximinez
reviewCommentsList.body: This is the wrong place to check if a transaction is supported. Transactions that come in from peers are never `Json`, and thus are never parsed as such. reviewCommentsList.author: dangell7
reviewCommentsList.body:
You fall through to `tecNO_PERMISSION` on some transactors and `tesSUCCESS` on others. 

If possible it would be helpful if you chose one or the other so that we can have consistency.

Furthermore, I believe if you flip this to fall through to tecNO_PERMISSION, which I would recommend, you don't actually need to get the trustline ledger entry or do any of those other checks.

reviewCommentsList.author: yinyiqian1
reviewCommentsList.body:
Checking granular permissions depends on the implementation details of the transaction. This transaction allows multiple properties of a trustline to be set within a single transaction.

For instance, if a delegated account has the granular permission to freeze a trustline (`TrustlineFreeze`) but not to unfreeze it (`TrustlineUnfreeze`), we can determine that if the unfreeze flag is set, the transaction should return tecNO_PERMISSION.
However, we cannot determine that setting the freeze flag returns tecSUCCESS, as it may also set other unauthorized flags or modify the trustline's limit, which is not permitted.

On the other hand, if a transaction only allows one action at a time, meaning the
